text:
Nora (FinOps): pinging @AWS Sales — we saw ~20% overage on committed GPU hours in eu-west-1 last month, need a root cause and request for retro credit if billing misattributed. cc @Alex @Sam :thinking_face:
AWS Sales: thanks Nora, I'm pulling the invoice now. can you paste the invoice lines and commitment id? I'll escalate to the capacity ops team.
Nora (FinOps): sure — invoice snippet:
```
Invoice: 4567123
Commitment: CMT-RED-2025-EU
Line: GPU-hours eu-west-1 (A100) x 10,000 => $120,000
Billed usage: 12,400 GPU-hours (overage 2,400)
Suspected cause: ~600 hours were billed at on-demand after preemptions/fallbacks during migration window
```
Sam (EngInfra): we had a rolling job migration 2025-03-12 -> 2025-03-14 that triggered autoscaler fallbacks when spot capacity thinned in eu-west-1b. logs show repeated preempt events + fallback to on-demand pools. snippet of autoscaler events:
```
2025-03-13T02:21Z scale-down: spot eviction
2025-03-13T02:22Z fallback: launch on-demand i-0abc.. (eu-west-1b)
2025-03-13T02:23Z job drain -> moved to on-demand
```
AWS Sales: ok that matches our usage metering — preemptions can cause fallback billing if instances transition to on-demand. For a retro credit we need (1) proof of autoscale fallback events (you sent that), (2) timestamps tied to the billed resources, and (3) a short writeup explaining your expected committed pool vs measured. we'll review with billing ops.
Morgan (SRE): quick Q — on future EDPs can we get hard capacity guarantees? We need p99 inference slots and minimum GPUs in eu-west-1 for production.
AWS Sales: public regions don't normally have fixed hard capacity guarantees. but we can add a "Capacity SLA Addendum" to an EDP: prioritized placement + soft capacity reservation. it usually carries a pricing uplift (~15%). alternative: Dedicated Hosts or a private pool in the region which gives stronger placement guarantees. also we can include a 72h ramp window for seasonal spikes.
Alex (Infra): 15% uplift is heavy. we prefer contractual ramping + burst credits instead of permanent uplift. proposed contract language: if vendor cannot provide >=90% of committed capacity in the region for a continuous window >72h, vendor issues credits equivalent to 2x the per-hour cost of missed GPUs and allows a one-time reallocation of up to 30% of committed capacity to another region at no penalty.
Nora (FinOps): also want monthly true-up (not annual) and ability to convert up to 30% of commitment into convertible credits to move between regions. want explicit multiplier for preemptible->on-demand fallbacks (e.g., if fallback causes on-demand billing, vendor should apply billed-at-on-demand minus committed-rate refund).
AWS Sales: noting asks. for the retro March credit — we'll need to correlate the job migration timestamps with the billing meter IDs. if billing ops accepts, expect a credit line in the next invoice cycle. for new EDP terms: draft options I can run by legal: 12 or 24 month base, 30% convertible pool, 10% burst buffer, capacity SLA addendum as optional (15% uplift) or credit-based SLA (your suggested credit language). I'll aim to return a term sheet by EOD.
Nora (FinOps): please also check whether any of the overage was double-counted during cross-AZ migration (we saw duplicate meter lines for 2025-03-13 02:22Z).
Billing Bot: Ticket #6421 created for invoice dispute (assign: billing-ops).
Sam (EngInfra): I'll attach autoscaler logs + cluster activity to ticket #6421 in a bit.
AWS Sales: appreciated — if you can attach pod/event IDs and the instance IDs we can map to meter lines faster.
Alex (Infra): one more ask: include a clause for advance notice + credits when a provider plans maintenance that could reduce available spot capacity in a region for >24h. we need predictable maintenance windows or migration support.
AWS Sales: noted. I'll push for maintenance-notice and migration support language in the term sheet. will follow up with a tracker doc and the draft by EOD. :thumbsup:
Nora (FinOps): thanks — will watch for the draft.
Morgan (SRE): thanks team, adding this to the risk register. :white_check_mark:
